brief.topic: When a Flag Is Usually a False Alarm

s01: Your message filter catches nine out of ten unwanted messages.
That sounds reassuring.
But when it flags a message, how often is the flag right?
Consider a made-up batch of one thousand messages.
Ten are unwanted, and nine hundred ninety are ordinary.
The filter catches nine of the ten unwanted messages.
Suppose it also flags one in ten ordinary messages.
That makes ninety nine false alarms.
Now look only inside the flagged tray.
There are nine unwanted messages and ninety nine ordinary ones.
Nine out of one hundred eight flags are right: about eight percent.
Catching most unwanted messages is a different question from trusting a flag.
Change the batch: now one hundred messages are unwanted and nine hundred are ordinary.
The filtering rates stay the same.
We get ninety true flags and ninety false alarms.
This time, half the flags are right.
Recall is the share of actual unwanted messages that we catch.
Precision is the share of flags that are right.
These are invented counts, not measurements of a real product.
When you read a model metric, ask which group is underneath the fraction.

scenes.narration:
Your message filter catches nine out of ten unwanted messages. That sounds reassuring. But when it flags a message, how often is the flag right?

Consider a made-up batch of one thousand messages. Ten are unwanted, and nine hundred ninety are ordinary. The filter catches nine of the ten unwanted messages. Suppose it also flags one in ten ordinary messages. That makes ninety nine false alarms.

Now look only inside the flagged tray. There are nine unwanted messages and ninety nine ordinary ones. Nine out of one hundred eight flags are right: about eight percent. Catching most unwanted messages is a different question from trusting a flag.

Change the batch: now one hundred messages are unwanted and nine hundred are ordinary. The filtering rates stay the same. We get ninety true flags and ninety false alarms. This time, half the flags are right.

Recall is the share of actual unwanted messages that we catch. Precision is the share of flags that are right. These are invented counts, not measurements of a real product. When you read a model metric, ask which group is underneath the fraction.
